name: Wind Power IoT Platform
tagline: Real-time turbine monitoring across 8 wind farms
background: Envision Energy needed a unified operations dashboard to monitor 2,000+ wind turbines spread across remote locations in China. The legacy system was batch-based, delivering data with 15-minute latency and no fault alerting — field engineers were flying blind.
technicalDecisions: Chose InfluxDB over TimescaleDB for its native time-series compression and continuous query features, achieving 10x storage reduction on raw telemetry
Adopted Kafka as the ingestion bus to decouple edge device producers from backend consumers, enabling replay and back-pressure handling
Built a Three.js WebGL component for interactive 3D turbine inspection — significantly cheaper to iterate on than procuring a dedicated SCADA 3D tool
Used MQTT over CoAP for edge devices because of better broker ecosystem support and QoS level flexibility
Implemented delta-compression on the client side so WebSocket frames stayed under 1KB even for batch telemetry bursts

name: Gate SEO Platform
tagline: Performance-first SEO analytics for a top-10 crypto exchange
background: Gate.io required an in-house SEO platform to track keyword rankings, backlink health, and Core Web Vitals across thousands of landing pages in 15 languages. Third-party SaaS tools couldn't handle the scale or provide the custom metrics the SEO team needed.
technicalDecisions: Chose Next.js App Router with ISR to serve pre-rendered SEO pages while keeping content fresh on a per-route revalidation schedule
Implemented a virtual list (TanStack Virtual) for the 100k-row keyword ranking table, keeping DOM node count under 500 at any time
Used Redis as a read-through cache in front of PostgreSQL for dashboard queries, cutting P99 query latency from 800ms to 120ms
Adopted WebSocket-based live ranking updates so the team could watch real-time SERP position changes during campaigns
Shipped a lightweight crawler microservice in Go to avoid Python GIL bottlenecks during concurrent page audits

name: Chaos Developer Platform
background: The engineering team was blocked by a centralised ops team for every deployment and environment request. Chaos was built to give developers full self-service control over deployments, feature flags, secrets, and on-call tooling — without needing to file tickets.
technicalDecisions: Built on top of ArgoCD GitOps model so every deployment is auditable and rollback is a single git revert
Chose Go for the platform API layer to minimise runtime overhead and binary size in Kubernetes sidecars
Implemented RBAC at the resource level (project / environment / action) using a custom policy engine inspired by Casbin
Unified feature flags, secrets, and config under a single 'environment context' abstraction so services only needed one SDK
Shipped an incident timeline view that auto-correlates deployment events with PagerDuty alerts — dramatically reducing RCA time
